jobs.title: Enterprise Engineering Systems Director
jobs.description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

Building on The Aerospace Corporation's reputation as a trusted, impartial advisor with integrity and dedication to mission success, the Civil Systems Group (CSG) combines deep technical expertise with market-leading innovation to help our customers solve complex systems engineering and integration challenges. CSG is organized by core customer-facing lines of business to manage and grow programs within NASA, NOAA, and the NNSA, while extending our capabilities to other civilian federal government agencies fully integrated within Aerospace rules, regulations, processes, values, and behaviors.

We are looking for an Enterprise Engineering Systems Director
(Systems Director – Systems and Digital Engineering)
. As a Systems Director in the Civil Systems Group within Defense, you will provide leadership, planning and direction to an experienced team of engineers and work closely with Engineering Technical Managers to support the mission area of the Department of Energy (DOE) National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) Office of Defense Programs (DP). You will lead and manage your team to accomplish systems engineering/analysis to various Defense Program tasks in support of our Nation. You will mentor your team to leverage Aerospace’s vast network of subject matter experts to bring innovative solutions to NNSA’s hardest problems. Additionally, you will look to identify new opportunities/challenges to leverage Aerospace capabilities to apply to our NNSA customer.

This is a full-time position based in Albuquerque, NM, Crystal City, VA, Colorado Springs, CO, or El Segundo, CA which requires a minimum of 4 days/week onsite work.

What You’ll Be Doing

Work closely with Principal Director and the rest of the management team to lead and manage Aerospace Enterprise Engineering team members with the challenging issues Aerospace is tackling for Defense Programs within the National Nuclear Security Administration.
Supports establishment of the Enterprise Engineering organization's objectives/goals with Principal Director and communicate them to your subordinates and interfacing organizations.
Provide strategic leadership and conducts activities consistent with corporate policies/practices, goals, and objectives.
Participates with higher management in determining the organization's structure and staff including resource needs (budget planning and allocation of resources).
Reports the organization's activities, progress, and achievements through written and oral reports to management, subordinates, and customers.
Coordinates work activities within the organization; monitors workload, work progress, and schedules; ensures completion of organization's work assignments within cost and schedule guidelines.
Seeks and identifies opportunities for additional, expanded, and new business and assists Sr. management in evaluating and pursuing new possibilities.
Cooperates and communicates frequently with customers to coordinate and report work progress, issues, and results.
Conducts staff performance reviews and recommends performance improvement, career development, salary, and promotion actions; establishes staffing needs; advises reassignments, training, transfers, and other staff deployments; and assists other supervisors in evaluating and assigning staff.
Directs technical group performing engineering design, analysis, or other research and development activities.
Lead from the front to influence customers to field more integrated solutions.

What You Need to be Successful - Systems Director – Systems Engineering and Digital Engineering

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor's degree in engineering, science, or another appropriate technical discipline
12 or more years of progressively responsible professional engineering/scientific experience
Experience in a managerial/leadership role with proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with all levels of contractors, customers, and corporate staff
Demonstrated networking, teaming, management, and leadership skills within a program office or matrixed technical organization, building and leading project teams, formulating task plans, ensuring product quality, and effectively interacting with customers.
Proven technical credibility across a broad set of systems engineering topics, and a deep understanding of the engineering of complex systems
Experience working with U.S. government agencies such as DOE/NNSA and DoD
Demonstrated strong interpersonal, organizational, written, and oral communication skills
Availability to travel domestically, up to 25% of the time
This position requires a current and active Top Secret or Q security clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance.

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

Advanced degree in engineering or math with specific experience in Systems/Digital Engineering
Familiarity with the DOE and NNSA National Laboratories in the Defense Programs Arena
Knowledge of the Aerospace Engineering and Technology Group (ETG) skills and capabilities
Demonstrated ability to create solutions to address national security needs
Holds a TS or DOE Q clearance with ability to obtain SCI

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. The grade-based pay range for this job is listed below. Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills.

Pay Basis: Annual

Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who:

Operate Strategically
Lead Change  
Engage with Impact  
Foster Innovation  
Deliver Results

Ways We Reward Our Employees

During your interview process, our team will provide details of our industry-leading benefits.

Benefits vary and are applicable based on Job Type. A few highlights include:

Comprehensive health care and wellness plans
Paid holidays, sick time, and vacation
Standard and alternate work schedules, including telework options
401(k) Plan — Employees receive a total company-paid benefit of 8%, 10%, or 12% of eligible compensation based on years of service and matching contributions; employees are immediately eligible and vested in the plan upon hire

to lead our team in building something great while influencing stability and quality of the technology. At Ibotta, our engineering team is organized cross-functionally by squads that build remarkable products for the company, including the platform powering our app that is used by millions of consumers. We’re looking for a director eager to drive a strong engineering vision, lead multiple teams, and scale the organization while fostering a collaborative, inclusive culture.

This position is located in Denver, Colorado as a hybrid position requiring 3 days in office (Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday). Candidates must live in the United States.

Not based in Denver? We will offer a relocation bonus to help make your move to the Mile High City a smooth one
.

What You Will Be Doing

Develop and deploy new strategies for building a highly engaged development organization that delivers predictably and in line with our emerging customer needs.
Inspire and mobilize individuals and teams to achieve results.
Ensure timely delivery of engineering solutions to meet business needs while providing a transparent view to progress.
Communicate technical concepts to business stakeholders as well as communicate business objectives to the technical team.
Collaborate across functional areas to define and prioritize technical solutions that support business needs, efficiencies, and revenue.
Collaborate with external partners to navigate partner onboarding, technical solutions, and development timelines.
Partner with Product Management and Architecture to prioritize, scope, and plan business milestones and set goals.
Foster an organization that understands how to balance technical debt vs. feature delivery.
Coach and develop engineering managers; address technical, resource, and personnel issues.
Support technical innovation and lead the creation, continual refinement, and active enforcement of our development standards to ensure that our technology enables a sustainable competitive advantage.
Build an organization with appropriately high technical competence that strives for excellence.
Identify opportunities where AI can replace manual processes or create new revenue streams, directly contributing to Ibotta's financial trajectory and competitive positioning.
Drive long-term technology strategy by treating AI as a core utility, championing data literacy and AI fundamentals across engineering, and identifying automation opportunities that multiply team productivity at scale.
Use AI to build solutions, quality of life improvements, team processes and production systems when able
Research new technologies to stay abreast of industry trends and standards.
Embrace and uphold Ibotta’s Core Values: Integrity, Boldness, Ownership, Teamwork, Transparency & A great idea can come from anywhere.

What We Are Looking For

5+ years of engineering management experience.
10+ years of experience in software engineering.
Experience managing managers, and leading multiple teams.
Experience collaborating with diverse stakeholders including customers, senior management, and other business leaders.
Skilled at agile software development and management.
Has had exposure to multiple languages and frameworks as either an engineer or manager.
Experienced with security, cost, performance, scale, and reliability strategies.
Highly effective performance manager and comfortable managing team members with different skill sets and technical expertise.
Motivated by a fast-paced and adapting environment.
Demonstrates effective written and verbal communication.
Has worked with cloud-based data architectures and platforms (AWS preferred) and experience with DevOps culture. DevSecOps is a plus.
Experience with event-driven architectures and platforms is a strong plus.
Understanding native mobile app development and frontend web development is a great extra!

Ibotta (NYSE: IBTA) is a leading performance marketing platform allowing brands to deliver digital promotions to over 200 million consumers through a network of publishers called the Ibotta Performance Network (IPN). The IPN allows marketers to influence what people buy, and where and how often they shop – all while paying only when their campaigns directly result in a sale. American shoppers have earned over $1.8 billion through the IPN since 2012. The largest tech IPO in history to come out of Colorado, Ibotta is headquartered in Denver, and is continually listed as a top place to work by The Denver Post and Inc. Magazine.

To learn more about what our Tech teams are doing day to day, visit Building Ibotta on Medium.com

This position is located in Denver, CO and includes competitive pay, flexible time off, benefits package (including medical, dental, vision), Employee Stock Purchase Program, and 401k match. Denver office perks include paid parking, snacks, and occasional meals.

jobs.title: Director, Technology & Innovation
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Director of Innovation leads TPI's technology development function, driving the creation and maturation of new and emerging technologies for composite wind blade design, materials, and manufacturing. This role owns the full technology pipeline — from early-stage concept and low Technology Readiness Level (TRL) research through TRL 8/9 qualification and Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL) 6 production implementation — while also scouting, evaluating, and deploying existing external technologies and solutions with applicability to TPI's production process. The Director builds and leads a team of engineers and technologists, sets the technology roadmap, and partners closely with engineering, operations, quality, and program management to convert innovation into measurable production impact.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Lead, build, and develop a team responsible for the development of new and low-TRL technologies across materials, processes, tooling, and automation for composite wind blade manufacturing.
Own technology maturation from concept through TRL 8/9 and MRL 6, establishing and managing stage-gate processes, milestones, and go/no-go criteria for each development program.
Identify, evaluate, and vet existing technologies and solutions (internal or external to TPI) for applicability and transferability to current production processes; lead build-vs-buy-vs-partner assessments.
Establish and maintain a technology roadmap aligned with business strategy, customer requirements, and manufacturing capability needs.
Champion the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning methods to accelerate technology development, modeling, process optimization, and decision-making.
Direct experimental design, testing, characterization, and numerical/physical modeling required to validate new technologies prior to production release.
Partner with Advanced Manufacting, engineering, operations, quality, and program management to plan and execute technology transitions into serial production with minimal risk.
Manage technology development budgets, timelines, resourcing, and external partnerships (universities, suppliers, national labs, technology vendors).
Build and protect TPI's intellectual property portfolio through disciplined invention disclosure, patent strategy, and technical documentation.
Develop business cases, cost-benefit analyses, and ROI models to prioritize and justify technology investments to senior leadership.
Mentor and develop engineering and technical staff, growing organizational capability in technology development, AI application, and composites manufacturing.
Represent TPI's technology function with customers, suppliers, industry groups, and at technical conferences.
Perform other related duties and special projects as assigned.

Required Qualifications (Education, Skills, and Experience)

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Materials, Aerospace, or Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field required; advanced degree preferred.
Minimum 10-15 years of progressive experience in technology/product development, R&D, or advanced manufacturing engineering, including significant experience leading technical teams or programs.
Demonstrated experience taking technologies through formal TRL/MRL (or equivalent stage-gate) maturation processes from concept to production.
Required AI literacy: demonstrated hands-on experience applying artificial intelligence and/or machine learning tools and techniques to engineering, R&D, or manufacturing problems, and working knowledge of how AI can be applied to accelerate technology development.
Strong background in composites, materials science, or advanced manufacturing processes; wind blade or wind energy industry experience strongly preferred.
Proven ability to scout, assess, and integrate third-party or existing technologies into an operating production environment.
Experience with numerical modeling, simulation, CAE/FEA tools, and experimental test design and characterization.
Strong leadership, team-building, and people-development skills, with experience managing engineers and technologists.
Ability to build and present business cases, technology roadmaps, and budget justifications to executive leadership.
Excellent verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills; verbal and written fluency in English.
Strong critical thinking, problem analysis, and hands-on, practical problem-solving abilities.
Ability to work effectively across a distributed, global organization and with cross-functional/multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
Direct experience in wind blade design, composites manufacturing, or renewable energy technology development.
Track record of patents, publications, or other intellectual property contributions.
Experience developing or deploying custom AI/ML models (e.g., predictive modeling, computer vision for defect detection, process optimization algorithms).
Formal program/project management training or certification (e.g., PMP).
Experience managing external partnerships with universities, national labs, or technology suppliers.
Familiarity with CAD/CAM and simulation tools such as ABAQUS or CATIA.

Travel Requirements

This position requires approximately 25-50% travel, depending on project needs, including visits to TPI manufacturing facilities, supplier and technology partner sites, testing facilities, and industry conferences. Travel may include both domestic and international destinations.

Location

This position is remote-eligible. Candidates based near El Paso, Texas are preferred, but highly qualified remote candidates will be considered.

This role oversees engineering design activities, coordination with third-party consultants and contractors, and the delivery of technical support throughout project development, procurement, construction, and commissioning.

Lead a multidisciplinary team of civil and electrical engineers and technical specialists
Continuously improve engineering design management processes
Forecast staffing needs based on active projects and future pipeline, and assign resources to support development and construction activities
Identify long-term resource requirements and recruit project engineering personnel
Act as a senior technical authority supporting development, M&A, and construction efforts, and manage external subject-matter experts as required
Review and resolve complex technical issues in collaboration with internal experts and external consultants
Develop and implement efficient engineering workflows focused on standardization and repeatable designs
Provide technical coordination with Operations Engineering, Development, Compliance, and Asset Management teams at various project stages
Ensure regulatory and compliance requirements, including NERC standards, are incorporated into project designs
Lead technical coordination with lenders’ independent engineers during design and construction phases

Bachelor’s degree in engineering required; electrical engineering preferred
Professional Engineering License

At least 10 years of experience in the energy industry
Minimum of 5 years of experience in utility-scale solar project engineering; BESS experience is a plus
Experience working in PJM and MISO markets is a plus
Background in civil and electrical design, medium-voltage collection systems, high-voltage substations, and SCADA for utility-scale solar projects
Experience supporting construction and commissioning activities
Experience preparing or reviewing construction cost estimates for similar projects

jobs.description:
Base Operations, Inc. | Washington, DC (Hybrid)

About Base Operations

Base Operations builds AI-powered physical threat intelligence software for global enterprises and U.S. federal/defense agencies. Our platform — including BaseEngine, BaseScore, and BaseCoPilot — helps security, risk, and operations teams understand and act on real-world threats faster than legacy intelligence tools allow. We're a dual-use company: the same core technology serves Fortune 500 security teams and U.S. government customers, which means our engineering org has to meet a high bar for both commercial velocity and federal-grade rigor.

We're a Series A company scaling fast, and this role is foundational to how we build, ship, and scale engineering as a discipline — not just as a function.

The Role

We're hiring a Head of Engineering
to own the technical backbone of our engineering organization. This is a hybrid IC/leadership role: you'll be hands-on enough to make real architectural decisions, structured enough to run delivery like a program, and fluent enough in modern AI tooling and workflows to help the team build with AI, not just build AI products.

You'll report into our CEO — and will be one of the senior-most technical leaders shaping how Base Operations' engineering team scales. You’ll work hand in hand with our VP Product who has established and is responsible for the delivery cadence, roadmap decision framework and overall product and engineering operating model that drives our unified dual use strategy.

What You'll Do

SimX is a fast-growing company that has brought virtual and augmented reality to medical simulation training. At the end of 2024, we were acquired by Madison Industries, a partnership that has provided a surge in resources to accelerate our growth and mission. jobs.description:
Teamwork makes the stream work.  
Roku is changing how the world watches TV
Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.
From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.

About the role
  Software engineering is at an inflection point — and Enterprise Engineering at Roku sits right at the center of it. Applications are increasingly built to plug into AI platforms — exposing their capabilities as services for agents rather than standing alone as siloed apps — and the once-clear lines between engineering disciplines are blurring, rewarding versatile engineers who can work across the stack and own outcomes end to end. At the same time, AI is raising the bar on what a lean engineering organization can deliver.  
Roku is seeking a Director of Software Engineering to lead the organization that builds the custom applications, integrations, enterprise data, AI and agentic capabilities, and productivity platforms that power how the company runs. This is a senior leadership role: you’ll set the technical vision, shape our architecture for an AI-native future, and make Enterprise Engineering’s systems agent-ready — all while championing engineering excellence in quality, security, and speed.  
Reporting to the VP of Enterprise Engineering, you will lead a global organization across teams in the US, UK, and India. You’ll own the software engineering organization building Roku’s custom enterprise applications, integrations, and enterprise data; Productivity Engineering, the platforms and workflows that shape how thousands of employees work each day; and enterprise AI enablement — the AI-enabled capabilities that let our systems and our people operate with far greater leverage.  
The ideal candidate is a builder-architect and a transformation leader. You have deep, current expertise in AI and software architecture and a clear point of view on where software is heading, and you have repeatedly reshaped teams and lifted engineering standards to meet that direction. You care as much about how work gets done — the architecture, the rigor, the ways of working — as about what gets shipped.  
For California Only - The estimated annual salary for this position is between $650,000 - $750,000 annually. Compensation packages are based on factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, certifications, and specific geographical location. This role is eligible for health insurance, equity awards, life insurance, disability benefits, parental leave, wellness benefits, and paid time off. 

What you’ll be doing
  Technical Direction & Architecture

Set the technical vision and standards for the software engineering organization that builds Roku’s custom enterprise applications, integrations, and enterprise data.  

Advance our architecture and engineering practices — driving cloud-native design, strong engineering and security discipline, and fast, reliable delivery.  

AI & the Agentic Platform

Drive our  enterprise AI enablement  strategy — building the reusable foundations for agent-ready systems (identity-aware MCP services, reusable skills, eval practices, and a governed  context layer) and enabling teams across the organization to build, adopt, and operate AI capabilities themselves.  

Lead the organization’s shift to AI-first engineering: drive team-wide AI adoption, create the psychological safety for teams to experiment and learn, redesign workflows around AI rather than bolting it on, and establish standards for the quality and accountability of AI-assisted work.  

Organization & Transformation

Reshape team topology around outcomes as the boundaries between engineering disciplines blur, evolving the org toward versatile, product-aligned teams.  

Build, coach, and uplift a high-performing, geographically distributed engineering team, and serve as a thought partner to executive leadership.  

Enterprise Scope & Governance

Own Productivity Engineering: the platforms, workflows, and tools that shape how thousands of employees collaborate, execute, and make decisions.  

Partner on the architecture and execution of major enterprise tentpole initiatives that span multiple systems and teams.  

Operate with the governance, security, audit, and compliance discipline (including SOX) that enterprise systems require.  

We’re excited if you have
  1 5 + years building and leading software engineering teams, including significant experience leading managers and/or senior engineers in an organization of scale.  

Deep, current expertise in cloud architecture and software engineering, with the judgment to set architectural direction and go as deep as a problem requires — whether as a hands-on architect or leading through strong managers.  

Personal, current fluency with the agentic engineering toolchain — conversational AI and agentic coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot) used across the full software development lifecycle — with the judgment to drive an agent, verify its output, and lead by example. Depth in LLM-based applications, agentic workflows, MCP integration, and eval-driven development.  

A track record of raising engineering standards in an existing organization — modernizing architecture, embedding secure-by-design practices, and improving quality, rigor, and agility.  

Conviction and experience in organizational design, including reshaping teams around outcomes and evolving operating models.  

Experience with enterprise or internal platforms and the governance, security, and compliance that come with them; large-scale enterprise system modernization is a strong plus.  

Change leadership: a demonstrated ability to move an organization to new, AI-enabled ways of working and to protect strategic capacity against the gravity of run-the-business work.  

Exceptional executive presence, a data-driven mindset, and the ability to influence senior stakeholders.  

How will I use AI at Roku?

At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We’re looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they’ve used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact.  
We value your AI skills if you’ve built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks — and you can describe projects where you shipped real work with these tools. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you.  
What's Roku's approach to hybrid working?
Roku fosters an inclusive and collaborative environment where teams generally work in the office Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance.

What are some of the benefits?
Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits include global access to mental health and financial wellness support and resources. Local benefits include statutory and voluntary benefits which may include healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), life, accident, disability, commuter, and retirement options (401(k)/pension). Employees are supported in taking time off, in accordance with local leave policies and other personal needs to support their evolving work and life needs. It's important to note that not every benefit is available in all locations or for every role. For details specific to your location, please consult with your recruiter.

Accommodations
Roku welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations and adjustments in accordance with applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please direct your inquiries to EmployeeRelations@Roku.com.

What should I know about Roku's culture?
Roku is a great place for people who want to work in a fast-paced environment where everyone is focused on the company's success rather than their own. We try to surround ourselves with people who are great at their jobs, who are easy to work with, and who keep their egos in check. We appreciate a sense of humor. We believe a fewer number of very talented folks can do more for less cost than a larger number of less talented teams. We're independent thinkers with big ideas who act boldly, move fast and accomplish extraordinary things through collaboration and trust. In short, at Roku you'll be part of a company that's changing how the world watches TV. 
We have a unique culture that we are proud of. We think of ourselves primarily as problem-solvers, which itself is a two-part idea. Softchoice, a World Wide Technology company, supports commercial and SMB markets in the U.S. and Canada.

Want to work with highly motivated individuals on high-performance teams? Join WWT today!

What is the Internal WWT IT Team, and why join?

The Internal WWT IT team is the backbone of our company’s technological infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations and continuous innovation. Our team is dedicated to managing and supporting the company’s technology infrastructure, ensuring the smooth operation of hardware, software, networks, and data systems, while providing top-notch technical support to employees.

By joining the Internal WWT IT team, you will play a crucial role in maintaining the efficiency and security of our IT environment, enabling the company to achieve its strategic goals. The Internal IT team offers the opportunity to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, where your contributions will have a direct impact on the company’s success. If you are passionate about technology and eager to take on new challenges, we encourage you to apply and join our team.

What will you be doing?

As a Senior Engineering Manager - AI Advanced Development
you will lead a new, deliberately small team that answers the AI questions nobody else in the organization owns. Executive asks and emerging technology come to this team; you take them, prove out in weeks what is real and what is not, and hand the answer to the team that will run it — or kill the bet and say clearly why.

This team does not run anything in production and does not own long-term support. That constraint is the point: it is what allows the team to move at the speed of the technology. Your job is to make sure every piece of work ends in a decision rather than a demo.

This is a hands-on role. You will manage the team and still build — writing code, running evaluations, and pressure-testing your engineers’ conclusions yourself rather than relying on status reports. You are the first hire on the team, and you will hire Applied AI Engineers who join you.

Exceptional communication is a core requirement of this role, and you will present findings and recommendations directly to executive leaders — often without an intermediary and often when the answer is not the one they were hoping for. You must be able to take a technically complex, uncertain result and give a senior audience a clear recommendation, the reasoning behind it, and an honest account of what you do not yet know.

Responsibilities

Take executive and stakeholder asks about emerging AI capability and turn them into scoped, time-boxed investigations that produce a defensible recommendation.
Run experiments to a decision in weeks - building the smallest credible thing that answers the question and resist the pull toward polish.
Kill bets early and publicly, with a clear, written rationale that the organization can learn from and reuse.
Package accepted work for handoff: reference implementation, evaluation results, known limits, operating assumptions, and a receiving team that has agreed to take it.
Stay hands-on — build, prototype, and evaluate alongside the team, targeting roughly 60% of your time in the work itself.
Maintain a working point of view on the frontier of applied AI: models, agent frameworks, retrieval and context strategies, evaluation methods, and tooling — and know when each is genuinely ready.
Design and run evaluations that separate real capability from demo-quality results, including cost, latency, reliability, and failure-mode analysis.
Partner with platform, product, security, and data teams early so that anything handed off can operated by the team receiving it.
Say no to work that belongs elsewhere — production ownership, long-term support, and steady-state feature delivery — and route it to the right team.
Present findings, tradeoffs, and recommendations directly to executive leadership — in writing and in the room — including the conclusions that are unwelcome.
Write clearly and concisely for a senior audience: short, decision-oriented documents that stand on their own without a walkthrough.
Coach and develop senior engineers through clear expectations, direct feedback, and servant leadership.

How This Role Is Measured

Success in this role is not measured in shipped features or systems under management. It is measured by decisions made, bets killed early, and handoffs accepted by the teams that receive them. If you need production ownership to feel that your work matters, this is the wrong role.

,

Required Qualifications

Strong software engineering background with the ability to build working systems yourself, not only direct others to build them.
Demonstrated experience building AI-native applications — LLM integration, agents, retrieval, evaluation harnesses, and automation workflows.
Track record of moving from an ambiguous question to a defensible technical recommendation on a short timeline.
Experience leading senior engineers, including hiring, setting technical direction, and holding a high bar.
Demonstrated judgment about when a technology is ready and when it is not — including examples of work you stopped, and why.
Proficiency with modern backend and cloud technologies (e.g., Python and/or JavaScript/TypeScript, APIs, event-driven systems, containerized deployment).
Experience designing evaluations for non-deterministic systems, and comfort reasoning about cost, latency, and failure modes.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with demonstrated experience presenting directly to executive leadership and defending a recommendation under scrutiny.
Ability to structure and communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to senior, non-technical audiences, and to state uncertainty plainly rather than hiding it.
High tolerance for ambiguity, and the discipline to time-box work rather than let it expand.
Willingness to hand work away once the question is answered, and to let another team own the outcome.
Solid understanding of Agile and iterative delivery models.
Deep alignment with and commitment to the WWT Core Values.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience will be considered.

Hybrid 3 days/week in NYC office

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own a core area of the Viam platform. You'll set the roadmap for your area, define how product and engineering make decisions together, and partner with senior leadership on strategy: what keeps developers from adopting Viam, which experiences become bottlenecks, and where physical AI and robotics are heading with respect to how software engineers get involved.

You have worked as a software engineer, which is a hard requirement here; the role sits close enough to the code that it does not work otherwise. Prior robotics or IoT experience isn't required, but you should be excited to work close to hardware and physical systems.

What you'll do:

Own the roadmap for your area of the platform, from problem definition through launch and adoption, and decide what ships, what waits, and what gets deprecated.
Collaborate on product strategy: what keeps developers from adopting Viam, and which experiences become bottlenecks or blockers.
Develop a view on where physical AI and robotics are heading, and what that means for how software engineers get involved.
Work with engineering leads on the decisions that shape platform architecture, like what belongs in the core, in the registry, or in an SDK.
Take new capabilities from 0 to 1 and stay on them through real customer deployments.
Own the developer experience for your area, including SDK ergonomics, API surface, docs, and onboarding.
Define success against developer adoption and second activations, and use that to decide what to build next and what to cut.
Bring what you learn from customers and Forward Deployed engineers back into the roadmap, and build the product practice itself as you go.

What you bring:

Experience as a software engineer, building and shipping production software used by real users, plus 8+ years in product management since. The engineering background is a requirement, not a preference.
Experience building developer-facing or infrastructure products like APIs, SDKs, or platforms, where the user is an engineer.
A track record of taking products from ambiguity to production, including migrations, deprecations, and breaking changes that real customers depend on.
Technical credibility with engineers. You can run the SDK yourself, read the code well enough to ask the right question, and hold your own in a design review.
